estonia.title: Flag of the Republic of Estonia

colors.note: Represents Estonia's lakes and sky, as well as loyalty, truth, and the ancient quest for freedom.
Symbolises the rich dark soil of the homeland and the historical hardships Estonians have endured.
Represents birch bark, snow, and the Estonian people's striving toward enlightenment and hope.

desc:
- Three horizontal bands of equal width: blue on top, black in the middle, and white at the bottom
- Created by students at the University of Tartu in 1881 as the banner of the Estonian Students' Society
- First adopted nationally in 1922, banned during Soviet occupation, and re-adopted on 7 August 1990
trivia:
- The flag was consecrated at Otepää parish church on 4 June 1884, a date now celebrated as the Estonian Flag Day
- The blue-black-white banner flew defiantly on Tall Hermann tower in Tallinn on 24 February 1989 as independence loomed
- Some Estonians interpret the colours as blue sky, dark soil, and birch trees — elements of the national landscape
